sessions.name: A
sessions.reply:
I moved the costs into `groceries.csv` and removed every price from `meal-plan.md`.

- **`groceries.csv`:** It has the columns `item,cost_usd`. There is one row per dinner, plus a total row of 78. The total row's label notes the estimate is for 2 people and ±15%.
- **`meal-plan.md`:** It now has only the day and dinner table, plus a note that it's planned for 2 people with pantry staples assumed. I left out the budget notes and the eating-out limit, since they mention dollar amounts.

I treated this as a standing rule for the workspace, so future changes to `meal-plan.md` will keep costs in `groceries.csv`.

sessions.name: B
sessions.reply:
Yes, the week's food stays well within $200. My estimate is about **$94**, give or take 15%, so roughly $80–$108. That leaves about $90 or more of headroom.

- **`meal-plan.md`:** It has the seven dinners for Nov 23–29. Saturday (Nov 28) is salmon, asparagus and couscous for four, and the other nights are for two. It has no prices, because I understood it to be shared with your partner and costs shouldn't appear there.
- **`groceries.csv`:** The per-dinner costs and the total are here. Saturday is about $34, up from $18 for two. The other six dinners come to $60.

These are my own rough estimates rather than live store prices. I haven't priced anything at a particular store. I also assumed the other six dinners are for two people, and I didn't include drinks, wine or pantry staples.
